children: Leading players operating in the marketplace for Affordable Care Act plans traded lower on Tuesday after the Trump administration announced plans to remove hundreds of thousands of people from the ACA public exchanges due to allegations of fraud.

The White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, led by Vice President JD Vance, plans to cancel subsidy payments for 750,000 individual accounts in ACA exchanges, alleging their enrollments were unauthorized and fraudulent.

The purge is set to target people who are unaware of their enrollments, earn an annual income exceeding 400% of the federal poverty level, or have employer-provided healthcare and are therefore ineligible for the program.
The cancellations, expected to save $2.2B in taxpayer money, are the latest to impact ACA exchanges, established under the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) in 2010.

This year, millions of Americans witnessed a sharp increase in their monthly health insurance premiums after the U.S. Congress failed to extend the tax credits granted in 2021 for those who buy insurance through the ACA exchanges.

The administration also plans to cut off hundreds of brokers and agents who wrongly signed ACA enrollees for government healthcare.
